component.name: Picocrypt NG
component.summary: A very small, very simple, yet very secure encryption tool

description.p: Picocrypt NG is a small, simple, yet very secure file encryption tool. It uses XChaCha20 for encryption and Argon2id for key derivation, with optional cascaded Serpent encryption in paranoid mode.
Features include Reed-Solomon error correction for data recovery, keyfile support, volume splitting, and a full command-line interface for scripting and automation.

ul.li: Added reviewed Russian translations for the desktop and native Android interfaces
Polished the compact desktop layout and fixed non-ASCII password advisory clipping and window-size drift
Compressed CLI and Android outputs now use truthful .zip.pcv names
Android startup removes stale temporary files, and cancelled operations no longer enter the successful save flow
Android 7.0+ remains supported on 64-bit ARM and x86-64 devices; v2.19 APKs no longer include 32-bit ABIs
Updated the desktop to Fyne 2.8 with clean shutdown of background UI workers
Updated the release toolchain to Go 1.26.5 and refreshed pinned dependencies
Release workflows refuse to overwrite existing assets and integrate fail-closed SignPath Authenticode submission and verification for Windows artifacts
Desktop GUI layout and output theming are fixed for the compact Linux desktop window
Windows installer upgrades now replace the installed GUI executable in place, detect a running app, and clean up the previous orphaned portable executable
Android release tasks can assemble unsigned release APKs for F-Droid source builds while official GitHub release builds still require maintainer signing secrets
Android gomobile AAR builds now use stable empty Go build IDs for native libgojni.so files, supporting reproducible APK comparison
Updated golang.org/x/image to v0.43.0 for TIFF decoder vulnerability fixes reported by govulncheck
Web app: paranoid mode, comments, keyfiles, Reed-Solomon, force-decrypt, and plausible deniability — byte-compatible with the desktop app
Web app: fully client-side and handles files up to 1 GiB; splitting, recursive volumes, and multi-file archives remain desktop-only
Web app: the file selector is re-enabled after a completed operation
Internal: unified, stricter static analysis across the codebase
Release artifacts are signed with keyless cosign and a GitHub build-provenance attestation
Desktop: advanced-settings tooltips no longer flicker or jump
Android: key material is zeroed after use, saved file names are sanitized, and cloud backup is disabled
Privacy: the app no longer writes log files to disk
Reliability: incomplete output is cleaned up if an operation is interrupted mid-stream
Android: encrypt a whole folder or multiple files at once, with a new Compress toggle
Android: optional screenshot protection (FLAG_SECURE) that also hides the app in recent apps
Cross-platform passwords are normalized to Unicode NFC so non-ASCII passwords work across operating systems
Android: smaller per-architecture release APKs alongside the universal APK
Linux: the AppImage is GPG-signed and ships delta-update (zsync) info
The compression and deniability passes now report speed and ETA
Reed-Solomon decoding rejects malformed input instead of panicking, and a split size that would overflow is rejected before encrypting
Android runs long operations in a foreground service and adds a verify-first decrypt option
New Linux AppImage package
Late Finder/AppKit batches of one open gesture on macOS extend the already-applied iCloud selection instead of replacing it
The window title no longer embeds the version, keeping one consistent application name across desktop environments
A compact About dialog now shows the application version and project link
Finder/Dock-opened iCloud files on macOS are collected across slow callbacks and applied after the selected files are ready
The Linux desktop entry keeps the reverse-DNS app identity while using a readable X11 window class for MATE/XFCE task grouping
Desktop, Snap, Windows, AppStream, CLI, and volume-header metadata now report v2.12 consistently
Opening multiple files from Finder or the Dock on macOS no longer drops files when the system delivers the same action in several batches
The Linux desktop file now uses the same application identity as the packaged app
Desktop, Snap, Windows, AppStream, CLI, and volume-header metadata now report v2.11 consistently
Safer temporary output cleanup that does not follow symlinks
Hardened archive extraction with path rechecks before writing
GUI race fixes for long-running operations
Clearer diagnostics for damaged protected header fields
Documented CLI kept-output exit code and reduced WASM support surface
Compatibility checks for existing v2 volumes and v2.08/v2.09 behavior
File associations: double-click .pcv files to open in decrypt mode on Windows / macOS / Linux
Linux: .deb installs MIME XML + .desktop + AppStream metainfo (Nautilus, Dolphin); Snap advertises handler
macOS: .app bundle declares UTI io.github.picocryptng.pcv + Apple Events handler (Finder cold-launch)
Windows: NSIS installer (Picocrypt-NG-Setup.exe) writes ProgID + registry associations alongside portable .exe
Cross-platform application/x-pcv MIME type canonicalized in dist/mime/application-x-pcv.xml
File-type icon: pcv-icon.svg + 6 PNG renditions (16/32/48/64/128/256) + multi-resolution .ico
Added Linux ARM64 build artifacts for both GUI and CLI
Updated Linux CI workflows to build/test amd64 and arm64 variants
Updated UPX from v5.0.2 to v5.1.0 in build workflows
Flathub-only packaging release with no application feature changes
Updated Flatpak launcher and cleaned up Flathub packaging metadata/assets
Updated Flatpak app ID to io.github.picocrypt_ng.Picocrypt-NG for Flathub compliance
Renamed Flatpak desktop and metainfo files to match the new app ID
Expanded Flatpak metainfo content and release metadata
Stdin/stdout streaming support for pipeline automation
Fixed data race in signal handler and improved buffer security
Improved error handling and test compatibility
Added comprehensive CLI documentation and CLI-only build mode
Implemented full CLI feature parity with GUI encryption operations
Added secure password stdin support and graceful signal handling
Improved extraction and compression handling with better naming
Enhanced UI readability and visual hierarchy
Automatically clears sensitive input fields after completion
Refactored into modular packages and switched to the Fyne toolkit
Added mobile support and v2 header authentication with HMAC-SHA3-512
Maintained backward compatibility with v1.x volumes
Maintenance release following v2.00
Dependency updates and stability improvements
First release in new Picocrypt-NG organization!
